rationale: One lever actually matters and it is enable_thinking. On this model enable_thinking: null is not off: a plain 300-token request emits reasoning chunks (ttfc null, reasoning=10) and with enable_thinking: true the model never emits a content token at all - 0 content chars and 2397 reasoning chars at max_tokens 900, still 0 content chars and 10583 reasoning chars in 16.7 s at max_tokens 3000, finish_reason length in every case. TTFC is null where TTFT is a normal 57-92 ms, which is exactly the signature of thinking rather than speed. Pinning it to false is worth a paired +7.1% decode on its own (171.72 -> 183.97 tps, interleaved n=5, depth and sampler held constant) and it is the difference between an answer and no answer. The whole-config paired test, defaults vs final, alternating blocks n=10 per arm, is 183.89 tps / 77.4 ms / 1704 ms against 161.22 tps / 74.2 ms / 1929 ms: +14.1% decode, -225 ms total, +3.2 ms TTFT. Nearly all of that 14% is the thinking pin, not tuning - honest read is that the model was shipped with an unusable thinking default and the fix is a configuration correction. MTP depth is the only genuine tuning gain and it is small: the forward+backward sweep across adaptive/1/2/3/4/6/8 puts fixed 4 first at 183.13 tps against 181.48 for adaptive, and two independent paired alternating-block head-to-heads (n=10 per arm each) give 182.96 vs 181.19 and 183.45 vs 182.14, so +0.7% to +1.0% - better on both decode and TTFT in the first test, better on decode but 1.2 ms worse on TTFT in the second. That is at the edge of noise and should not be quoted as a win; it is kept because it never hurt and because the curve has a hard cliff above it (depth 6 costs 11%, depth 8 costs 33%), which matters for anyone tempted to raise it. mtp_num_hidden_layers is 1 here, unlike the gemmas' 4, which is why the plateau is at 3-4 rather than 4-6. KV quantization is rejected on all four arms: 8-bit+skip_last 185.81 tps, 4-bit+skip_last 176.84, 4-bit no-skip 177.69, against 190.96 for off, for a memory saving the model does not need at 40.5 GB resident of ~101 GB. Notably the documented turboquant_skip_last false hard runtime error under MTP did not reproduce here - it loaded and served three coherent streamed requests with no SSE error - so that failure mode is gemma-specific and was recorded as such, not copied forward. Context window is a true no-op at both a 47-token and an ~8k-token prompt (0.6 ms and 0.1 ms paired deltas). ANE prefill, the one model-specific lever nothing previously tuned exercised, is a genuine null: the kernels do compile and run (server log shows 142 ANE procedures warmed, 41 MLP and 30 GDN procedures eagerly compiled into 2 instance-pinned ANE programs) but it produced no TTFT or decode gain at a short prompt, at --context-pad 8000, at --context-pad 32000, or on a cache-defeated cold ~21.7k-token prefill (16673.6 ms off vs 16741.7 ms on, n=6 per arm). The apparent short-prompt ANE win in one head-to-head was a cold block-1 arm and was discarded, not reported. Sampling is throughput-neutral by construction and the coding sampler is kept on the model card's recommendation, not on a speed claim; the harness cannot even validate it because measure.py always sends its own temperature and force_sampling is false. The force_sampling apparent +4.2% is a measurement artifact - it overrides the harness's temperature 0.0 with the model's 0.6 - and is rejected.
failure_modes: The paged prefix cache serves the entire prefill under measure.py: the server logs 'Prefix cache restore ... cached=41001 suffix=7 blocks=11', so TTFT measures cache restore rather than prefill and every prefill-path knob reads null. Worked around with tuning/coldprefill.py, which prepends a fresh random nonce per request so cached_tokens stays 0.

turboquant_skip_last false with KV quant on did NOT produce the documented hard runtime error under MTP on this model. It loaded and served three coherent streamed requests (pad 0/300 tok, pad 8000/300 tok, pad 0/900 tok) with error null. Recorded as 'did not reproduce', not as the gemma failure.

auto_unloaded true does not reload. mtp_fixed_depth, qwen35_ane_prefill_enabled and turboquant_kv_enabled all PUT back requires_reload true + auto_unloaded true + auto_reloaded false; the model must be re-POSTed to /load and polled, and the auto-unload is asynchronous so loaded can still read true for a moment. Skipping the load fakes a ~2700 ms TTFT.

A single cold block can manufacture a verdict: the short-prompt ANE head-to-head had block-1 arm A at 164 tps against ~183 everywhere else, which alone produced an apparent +5.5% ANE win. Check per-sample lists, not just arm medians.

tuning/coldprefill.py v1 reported 4.7 tps for a request the server timed at 142.7 tok/s, because this server coalesces the SSE stream (11 chunks for 300 tokens) and the elapsed span included the prefill. Fixed to read generation_tokens_per_second from the per-request usage block. Any harness that counts SSE chunks here will be wrong by ~28x.
enable_thinking null is not off: it emits reasoning chunks while measure.py reports ttfc=None and a normal-looking ttft_ms. ttfc null with a healthy ttft_ms is thinking, not speed.

measurement_caveat: No number in this report is comparable to a number from a different block. Absolute decode throughput on this machine drifts 30%+ between sessions with no config change. Every verdict above is a paired comparison inside one block: interleaved A/B (tuning/ab.py) for knobs that do not reload (context window, sampler, force_sampling, enable_thinking); alternating blocks with a discarded warmup per block (tuning/block.py) for knobs that do reload (MTP depth, KV quant, ANE prefill, and the whole-config head-to-head); forward-then-backward ordering (tuning/sweep.py) for multi-value sweeps. baseline.json (single-block, 3 runs) and final-runs.json (single-block, 5 runs) are recorded for completeness and are NOT a comparison - the defaults-vs-final comparison is tuning/block-baseline-defaults-vs-final-config.json, n=10 per arm, and it is the only number to quote for the pair. The +14.1% is honest for 'defaults as shipped vs final config' but it is dominated by pinning enable_thinking off; against a hypothetical default with thinking already off the delta is ~1%, which is the MTP-depth margin and is at the edge of noise.
